Theme

Nature & food · Household, washing & chores

grow verb

plants, a beard

also grow vegetables, cultivate, grow a beard, grow one’s hair, plant (verb), plant a field, till (the soil)

classical

Cic. Fin. 4.38: vītem (Lewis & Short)
Ov. Met. 14.624: hortōs (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 166, 394

colō, colere, coluī, cultum

verb, third conjugation

grow, cultivate (plants, a field, a garden)

Of tending crops through the year: vītem, pōma, hortum colere. Putting them in the ground is serere.

Other words

  • serō, serere, sēvī, satum — sow, plant

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Caecilius in Cic. Sen. 24: serit arborēs; Varr. RR 1.35.1: serere līlium et crocum; Traupman 166

  • barbam (capillum) prōmittere — grow a beard (one’s hair), let it grow

    phrase: prōmittō, let grow · also used · classical · Liv. 6.16.4: multōs mortālēs capillum ac barbam prōmīsisse; Caes. BG 5.14.3: capillōque sunt prōmissō

    In Livy men let hair and beard grow in mourning; prōmissus is long, of hair or a beard (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • laudātō ingentia rūra, exiguum colitō

    praise big farms; farm a small oneVerg. G. 2.412–413

  • serit arborēs, quae alterī saeclō prōsint

    he plants trees to be of use to the next generationCaecilius in Cic. Sen. 24

  • spēs ūnica imperiī populī Rōmānī L. Quīnctius trāns Tiberim … quattuor jūgerum colēbat agrum

    the one hope of Rome’s empire, Lucius Quinctius, farmed a plot of four acres across the TiberLiv. 3.26.8

  • agrum cōnserere

    to plant a fieldTraupman 166

See also sow, tend the garden, garden, harvest, grow.
